office.label: Downtown Denver
office.oneLineDistinction: Towers, government and civic institutions in the central core
office.shortDescription: Downtown concentrates Denver’s traditional office towers, government functions, convention activity and cultural institutions within the central street grid. It offers the city’s most recognizably urban office setting, distinct from LoDo’s older warehouse blocks and Cherry Creek’s lower-scale office and retail mix.
worthKnowing: Building age and street activity vary across the core.

office.label: LoDo
office.oneLineDistinction: Historic warehouse blocks adapted for office, dining and retail
office.shortDescription: LoDo pairs Denver’s oldest commercial blocks and former warehouses with offices, restaurants, hotels and entertainment near Union Station. The smaller blocks and adapted buildings give it a different feel from the tower-heavy business core, while visitor and evening activity make it relevant to both office and customer-facing searches.
worthKnowing: Floorplates and building systems vary in adapted properties.

office.label: Cherry Creek
office.oneLineDistinction: Destination retail paired with professional offices and services
office.shortDescription: Cherry Creek combines a major shopping destination with professional offices, restaurants and personal services in a polished, lower-scale district southeast of Downtown. Retail centers and street-facing shops coexist with office buildings, making it useful for customer-facing firms that want a commercial setting unlike Denver’s central business core.
worthKnowing: Confirm whether a location sits within Denver rather than nearby Glendale.

industrial.label: Northeast Denver Industrial
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Warehouse and production areas within Denver’s northeast employment land
industrial.shortDescription: Northeast Denver contains broad employment areas with warehouse, distribution, manufacturing and service-industrial buildings. It is a City-of-Denver operating context, not a label for Aurora or Commerce City inventory. Larger sites and conventional industrial formats distinguish it from RiNo’s converted and mixed-use blocks.
worthKnowing: Verify municipality and exact operating attributes for each property.

industrial.label: RiNo
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Creative businesses and adapted industrial buildings north of Downtown
industrial.shortDescription: RiNo’s former industrial blocks now mix studios, creative offices, food and beverage, production businesses and newer development. Its retained warehouses and active street-level uses create a hybrid setting: more production-rooted than Downtown, but more mixed and customer-facing than Denver’s outer industrial areas.
worthKnowing: Industrial compatibility and building capability vary block by block.
